zip_caveats: ZIPs do not map to Harris County ballots. For your exact ballot, enter your name and address at harrisvotes.com/Voter/Whats-on-my-Ballot. Inside Houston, all of these lines split ZIP codes: nine congressional districts on this ballot (CD-2, 7, 8, 9, 18, 22, 29, 36 and 38, redrawn in 2025); state Senate Districts 4, 11, 13 and 18 (Houston's other Senate seats are not up this year); 24 state House districts (HD-126 to 135 and HD-137 to 150); State Board of Education Districts 4, 6, 7 and 8; county commissioner precincts (only Precincts 2 and 4 vote for commissioner this year, so Precinct 1 and 3 voters see no commissioner race); and justice of the peace Precincts 1 to 8 (each votes for its Place 2 judge). There are no constable races in Harris County this year. School districts cross ZIPs too. Most of Houston is in Houston ISD, which has nothing on this ballot. Cy-Fair, Klein, Spring, Sheldon, Tomball, Huffman, Crosby and New Caney ISDs each reach part of the city and do have races or measures; Aldine, Alief, Spring Branch, Katy, Humble, Clear Creek, Pasadena, Galena Park, Deer Park, Goose Creek, Conroe and Fort Bend ISDs also reach parts of Houston but have nothing on the Harris County ballot. City of Houston Prop A is only for people who live inside the city limits. A Houston mailing address in unincorporated Harris County does not count, and separate cities surrounded by Houston (for example Jersey Village in 77040, West University Place in 77005, and the Memorial Villages in 77024) do not vote on it. Parts of Houston lie in Fort Bend and Montgomery counties; those residents get a different county ballot that this guide does not cover, though they still vote on Prop A. Everything countywide (county judge, county attorney, clerks, treasurer, county school trustees, appraisal district, every district, county and probate court, and the 1st and 14th Courts of Appeals) is on every Harris County ballot. The ZIP list here is a convenience list of ZIPs that are mostly inside the city, not an official crosswalk; several include other cities or unincorporated areas.
notes: Harris County uses vote centers: any registered Harris County voter can vote at any Harris County vote center, early or on Election Day. Early voting runs Mon Oct 19 to Fri Oct 30: Monday to Saturday 7 AM to 7 PM, Sunday Oct 25 noon to 7 PM. Election Day, Tue Nov 3, is 7 AM to 7 PM. Bring your printed or handwritten notes into the booth (take them with you when you leave). Phones and other devices cannot be used inside the voting room. Texas has no straight-ticket voting, so you mark every race one by one; the Harris ballot is long (four of five races are judges), and skipping a race is fine. There is no Houston mayor or city council race on this ballot; Prop A is the only City of Houston item. Have a mail ballot and want to hand it in? On Election Day only, 7 AM to 7 PM, take it with your photo ID to 1019 Congress St, Houston 77002. Only you can drop off your own ballot. Questions: the mail ballot line, 713-755-3150. Harris's vote center map shows the wait at each site: tap a pin. After Oct 30, flip its switch to Election Day.
